text:
alex_support: FYI — customer acct_9a2f reporting promo credits behaving weirdly. They say promo credits (PROMOQ4) should have been used first but invoice shows paid usage charged and promo balance reduced after. Also promo expiration date on dashboard (Dec 1) != promo metadata (Nov 1). Can someone triage?

maria_billing: @alex_support thanks — can you paste the customer billing_profile id and the invoice id? and any screenshots the user sent?

alex_support: billing_profile bp_87d3, invoice inv_2025_11_0302 attached (screenshot). User screenshot shows dashboard promo balance: 100 credits remaining, expiry: 2025-12-01. API invoice shows credits applied: 0.00 and total charged: $18. All from same usage window.

alex_support: quick repro steps the user gave: 1) applied promo code PROMOQ4 on 2025-10-28 via console; 2) made API calls 2025-11-02 -> 2025-11-03 (embeddings + chat); 3) saw charges on invoice dated 2025-11-03, while promo balance dropped only after invoice posted. They think credits burned out of order.

ryan_engineer: pinging infra — can you attach the usage logs for acct_9a2f for 2025-11-02..03? I want to check token attribution order. Also which ledger entries correspond to the invoice id?

billing_bot: ledger entries for inv_2025_11_0302: [txn_991a debit $18, promo_adjust promo_PROMOQ4 -100credits applied 2025-11-03T02:14:09Z]. (automated)

lina_support: I pulled the user screenshots and console export. The console UI shows promo expiry 2025-12-01 but the promo meta (from promotions service) lists expiry 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z. Looks like a timezone/display mismatch, but that wouldn't explain burn-order.

ryan_engineer: initial hypothesis: redemption priority logic might be falling back to paid balance when promo bucket TTL is near expiry — there was a recent change in the billing worker to avoid sending negative balances to downstream invoice generator. I'll try to reproduce on staging. Repro steps I'll use: 1) create acct test_promo_priority; 2) add two buckets: paid_balance $50, promo_PROMOQ4 100credits with expiry 2025-11-01; 3) generate usage spikes to consume ~120 credits; 4) check ledger ordering and invoice generation.

maria_billing: if this is a bug we need to issue a manual credit ASAP before finance posts final invoice. Can you confirm whether invoice inv_2025_11_0302 is final or in draft?

billing_bot: invoice inv_2025_11_0302 status: finalized (2025-11-03T05:12:00Z). (automated)

lina_support: re: expiry mismatch — front-end reads expiry from promotions display service which applies account timezone shift incorrectly (local +30 days). I'll open a patch for display fix. For the burn-order: I reproduced on staging — when promo expiry < now+24h the redemption engine marks bucket as "low-TTL" and deprioritizes it (recent change), causing paid balance to be consumed first.

alex_support: not good — user expects promo to be consumed first until it actually expires. That policy should be explicit but current behavior is surprising.

ryan_engineer: root cause: commit 9f3b2 changed the burn priority to avoid mid-invoice negative promos. The worker uses this SQL to pick bucket in order: ```SELECT id, type FROM credit_buckets WHERE account_id=$1 ORDER BY expires_at ASC NULLS LAST, priority DESC;``` which pushes near-expiry promos to the front but then a separate filter `AND ttl_remaining > INTERVAL '24 hours'` was added; bug is priority inversion when ttl < 24h — code will mark as not usable for automatic redemption. I'll submit PR to revert that filter and add safety checks in billing exporter.

maria_billing: next steps: (1) issue manual adjustment to acct_9a2f for the overcharge amount ($18) as credit, (2) refund if charge already processed, (3) inform finance and ops. @ryan_engineer can you add the staging repro logs and proposed patch link?

ryan_engineer: will do. repro logs: ```2025-11-03T02:12:43Z usage acct_9a2f tokens=842 model=gpt-4x; 2025-11-03T02:12:44Z redemption attempted -> bucket paid_balance used; promo_PROMOQ4 skipped ttl_remaining=20h``` attaching full trace in Jira BRG-591. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/billing/pull/248 (wip).

lina_support: I'll prepare a customer-facing note explaining both issues: (a) UI expiry display bug (timezone) and (b) promo burn-order behavior caused by TTL safety filter. Recommend immediate manual credit and set promo TTL to +7 days to avoid automatic deprioritization while we patch.

maria_billing: Confirmed I'll create a finance ticket to reverse the charge if already captured. Charging team — please pause any automated collections for acct_9a2f until we resolve.

alex_support: I'll reply to the customer with expected timeline: manual credit in 4 business hours, patch to be merged and deployed to staging today, prod rollback/patch early tomorrow.

billing_bot: action created: ticket FIN-441 created, assigned to maria_billing. (automated)

maria_billing: tagging this as P1 for billing compliance. Closing loop once refund/credit done and PR merged.

ryan_engineer: adding note: promo lifecycle should treat promo as usable up to expiry inclusive. I'll include unit tests covering timezone boundary (UTC midnight) and ttl edgecases.

alex_support: thanks team. I'll update thread with customer reply and mark for follow-up after FIN-441 completes.
